subject: german
title: Theme 1: Evolution of German Society
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Theme 1: Evolution of German Society in A-Level German.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on Theme 1: Evolution of German Society.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Theme 1: Evolution of German Society.

concepts.def: The changing family: rising divorce, blended and single-parent families, and new family models in German-speaking society.
The digital world: how the internet, smartphones and social media are reshaping daily life and relationships.
Migration into German-speaking countries and its effects on society, the economy and culture.
Integration: how newcomers become part of society, debated alongside multiculturalism and identity.
Equality, especially between men and women, in work, family and public life as a current social trend.
Demographic change: an ageing population and falling birth rate, with major social consequences.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 1: Evolution of German Society — a core area of A-Level German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 1: Evolution of German Society brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 1: Evolution of German Society.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does 'die Familie im Wandel' describe?
options: The changing nature of the family in society
A family holiday
A type of house
A German verb
Equality (e.g. between men and women)
A train timetable
A school subject
A type of food

mcqs.q: Which is an example of 'der demografische Wandel'?
options: An ageing population and low birth rate
A new mobile phone
A football match
A music festival

mcqs.q: 'Die Migration' as a social trend means:
options: The movement of people into the country
A bird species
A grammar rule
A holiday abroad
A school subject
Equality (e.g. between men and women)
A type of house
A train timetable
